Standard: The integrated propulsion system is free of instabilities resulting from flow disturbances generated by the inlet, inlet duct, and secondary air systems located in the inlet. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review integrated propulsion system geometry to identify potential sources of total pressure distortion, total temperature distortion, swirl distortion, and planar waves. Analysis.
  (1) Verify that the inlet can provide the total mass flow demanded by the engine, bleeds, ECS, bay ventilation, and any other mass flow required by the air vehicle. The inlet should be able to provide mass flow to all secondary airflow systems that use airflow from the inlet, throughout the ground and flight envelope, without creating instability-inducing distortion or airflow deficit to the engine.
  (2) Characterize dynamic total pressure inlet distortion, steady-state swirl distortion, temperature ramp and spatial distortion, and planar wave distortion and include in the engine stability audit with the corresponding engine sensitivities.
  (3) For configurations with observed planar wave content (supersonic inlet buzz and subsonic planar wave distortion), quantify planar wave airflow limits from ground test data. For methodology and instrumentation details refer to SAE AIR5866 and SAE ARP6420. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct sub-scale wind tunnel tests to measure inlet dynamic total pressure, swirl, and planar wave distortion. For methodology and instrumentation details refer to SAE AIR1419, SAE ARP1420, and SAE ARP6420. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Test.
    (2) Lab test: For swirl distortion, compliance can be shown by examination if the engine is equipped with inlet guide vanes. For swirl methodology and instrumentation details, refer to SAE AIR5686 and SAE ARP6420.
    (3) Flight test: Conduct flight tests to verify inlet operability and propulsion system stability. Instrument flight test air vehicle with an AIP rake. For methodology and instrumentation details, refer to SAE AIR1419, SAE AIR5867, SAE ARP1420, and SAE ARP6420.
